INFR11269 Coursework: group - report marking rubric 
The group report is marked out of 100 and contributes   70%   of the coursework mark. ASR and RAG 
are assessed together. The video provides supporting evidence of the group's work and 
understanding; it receives no separate mark.

Total   100 
A substantive, well - explained investigation is more valuable than a long list of loosely connected 
features. Improvement over the baseline is not itself a scoring criterion: convincing analysis of a 
negative result can score highly. 
Performance descriptions 
The ranges below describe performance within each criterion. For example, performance assessed at 
70% in a 30 - mark criterion receives 21 marks. Markers select a position within the range according to 
the strength and completeness of the evidence. 
Technical work and system understanding 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
Substantial, technically rigorous work with sustained depth of understanding. Justifies 
the design against credible alternatives and explains important component 
interactions, constraints and failure modes precisely. Demonstrates independent 
reasoning about how and why the system behaves as it does. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
Technically sound, substantive work with a well - defined question. Explains the 
implementation and important system interactions accurately and justifies the main 
design choices. Some critical comparison or reasoning is present, but depth is not 
sustained across the important decisions. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
A coherent contribution addressing a clear question, with a mostly correct explanation 
of the implementation and main components. Demonstrates practical understanding, 
but design choices are largely asserted or described, with limited reasoning about 
alternatives and interactions.

2 
Performance level   Description 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
Some relevant implementation and basic understanding are demonstrated, but the 
contribution is limited or incompletely explained. Significant gaps in correctness, 
design justification or understanding of component interactions weaken the technical 
account. 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
Insufficient evidence of a coherent technical contribution or dependable 
understanding. Major errors, missing explanations or largely unexamined use of 
supplied components prevent the reader from establishing how the proposed work 
operates. 
Experimental design and evidence 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
A rigorous evaluation that isolates the effects central to the question. Uses well - 
justified baselines and metrics, checks material confounds and measurement 
reliability, and selects targeted tests that challenge the main claims. Evidence is 
sufficient to establish both the result and its limits. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
Well - designed, controlled comparisons with appropriate quality and cost metrics. 
Reports the conditions and measurement boundaries needed to assess the results, 
and addresses the main reliability concerns. Evidence supports the central 
comparison, although testing of its robustness or limits is less developed. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
A competent baseline comparison with relevant quality and cost measurements and 
reasonably clear conditions. Establishes the main result, but evaluation coverage is 
narrow or important controls and reliability checks are incomplete. The evidence 
supports only a limited claim. 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
Some relevant comparisons and measurements are provided, but incomplete 
controls, weakly justified metrics or unclear measurement conditions leave substantial 
uncertainty. Evidence is too limited or inconsistent to establish the central comparison 
convincingly. 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
The evaluation does not establish a credible comparison. Essential baselines, 
measurements or conditions are missing, or major methodological problems make the 
reported results unsuitable as evidence for the investigation. 
Analysis and conclusions 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
Develops a convincing explanation of the findings by connecting evidence to system 
mechanisms and discriminating between plausible explanations. Derives insightful 
implications for quality - cost trade - offs, tests the boundaries of the interpretation, and 
reaches precise conclusions whose scope is justified by the evidence. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
Provides reasoned explanations of the main findings, connects them to relevant 
system mechanisms and evaluates the important trade - offs. Conclusions are well 
supported and material limitations are examined, although alternative explanations or 
wider implications are not explored with sustained depth. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
Interprets the principal results correctly and draws conclusions broadly supported by 
the evidence. Identifies relevant trade - offs and limitations, but explanations remain 
conventional or partly descriptive, with limited examination of why the findings occur 
or when they would change. 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
Offers some plausible interpretation, but largely restates results or relies on untested 
explanations. Important trade - offs and limitations are insufficiently examined, and 
conclusions are only partly supported or insufficiently qualified.

3 
Performance level   Description 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
Provides little defensible analysis of the findings. Major claims lack supporting 
reasoning, important contrary evidence is ignored or misunderstood, or conclusions 
substantially exceed what the investigation establishes. 
Report communication 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
An exceptionally precise and economical report in which structure, terminology and 
visual presentation make a complex argument readily assessable. Claims, methods 
and evidence can be traced without reconstruction; figures and tables are self - 
contained and purposefully selected. No material ambiguity or avoidable distraction 
weakens the account. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
A well - organised, concise and technically precise report. The argument and its 
supporting evidence are easy to follow, with effective figures, tables and references. 
Minor ambiguities or uneven presentation remain, but do not materially obstruct 
assessment. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
A clear, complete and reasonably organised account with readable figures, tables and 
references. The main argument can be followed, but repetition, imprecise wording or 
uneven explanation requires occasional reconstruction of how methods, results and 
claims connect. 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
The basic account is understandable, but recurring problems with organisation, 
terminology, figures or referencing obscure important connections. Readers must 
reconstruct substantial parts of the argument or search for information needed to 
interpret the evidence. 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
Serious omissions or persistent presentation problems prevent reliable assessment of 
the work. The argument is difficult to reconstruct, or essential methods, results and 
supporting references cannot be located or interpreted. 
How the video is used 
Staff use the demonstration and explanations, including the answers in the final two minutes, to 
support assessment   of the report . The video can clarify the written account; the report must contain 
the central experimental evidence and argument. 
Video production polish, the number of speakers and how speaking time is divided do not attract 
separate marks. Clear, audible explanations and legible demonstrations allow staff to assess the work.
